notes.title: Private Matches Update
notes.notes:
Hey, fam! 
Time runs fast and it's been 4 months already from the start of the new Season.
With Season 2, we added new Sumo Wrestlers, arenas, and a lot of emotes!
Since last update, we kept working on the game, fixing bugs, and some other minor stuff.
But that's not all. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/4a3dc882bab6db2bf572c2da419e6ee432b42040.png

We developed a new feature  a lot of you asked for.
We dived in our feedback list from the community, and one of the most requested features was... playing with your friends only!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/41d6936c4bec86082619e236774bec592280ab1c.png

PRIVATE MATCHES
For that reason for the new update, we implemented private matches!
Now you can play with your party, without matching with other players online!
You can find this new mode right next to the other two :)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/fe3ff00980d67b4fe79571598908250449a3ba3e.png

THANKS SUMO WRESTLERS
We want to thank all the players playing since the Early Access and the newer ones that every day give Circle of Sumo a chance.
Thanks to all the players that created a Heya and played together to win the weekly Heyas' contest, because as you may know, COSOR is MUCH BETTER with friends😉
A special mention goes to the two Heyas that I sincerely had a lot of fun watching stealing the first place from each other:
Weslegang's Heya and  Alextheworst's Heya, thanks for the fun pals!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/a0f53127a5581f5a7219ef9f012c7dcb2171553d.png

DISCOUNT ON RYOs PACKS!
Starting tomorrow, Friday 11th, to Sunday 13th, all the RYOs packs will be 50% off!

DAILY TOURNAMENTS REMOVED
Last but not least we removed the daily tournament as not a lot of players were participating.

WHAT DO YOU THINK?
So what do you think about this last update? Are you hyped for the new private match mode of Circle of Sumo?
Let us know in the comments below, any feedback will be so helpful for future updates!

That's all, 
See you soon Sumotoris!

notes.title: Changelog 1.5.8 - Ranking System
notes.notes:
Hi, fellow sumotoris!

We received a lot of feedback regarding our ranking system and its balancing. Thanks to it, we developed a new version of our system. 

There will be no more negative points in case of winning, but we will still take rounds into account, so winning 5-4 will give you fewer points than winning 5-0.

It will also give slightly more points to the winner (and you will lose more points as a loser), so it will be easier to move from one rank to another.

We hope you enjoy the new system; we are eager to receive your feedback to improve it even further!

notes.title: Changelog 1.5.7 - Matchmaking
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!
With this small yet important update, we added a new fix to the matchmaking system solving an issue for players without a party trying to join FFA matches.

We are working hard on the matchmaking issues you guys are reporting. There still are a few corner cases we need to address but we are a step closer to have a perfectly smooth experience!

Changelog:

Fixed Free For All matchmaking for players without a party not starting with the minimum amount of players checked in, leading to longer matchmaking queue times


Have fun!

notes.title: Changelog 1.3.14
notes.notes:
Hi fellow sumotoris!

After last week release of the new tournament mode we've adjusted a few things:

Features: 

  Tournaments can now specify how many rounds you need to win a single match. This is on our end and it translates with: in the daily tournaments, the ones that happens every 4 hours, phases will now be played on a single match (instead best of 3) with 10 rounds per match!
  Added a button to show the brackets while waiting for the opponent to join the tournament

Fixes:

  Fixed some layout issues and typos in the UI

notes.title: In-game Live Tournaments Update!
notes.notes:
Our biggest update ever is out right now!
With the Live Tournament update you will be finally able to join in-game live tournaments  24/7!

HOW DOES IT WORK
Well, it's very simple! This is how we'll start.
Every 4 hours a tournament will start and the participant will compete in real-time.
The participants have to signup to the tournament in advance and each tournament has a maximum of 8 players competing.
There is a MON entry fee and, on the other side, a MON prize for the winner!


A STEP BY STEP WALKTROUGH


I'll explain everything with the help of some screenshots.
First of all, we added a BIG RED BUTTON SAYING LIVE TOURNAMENT as you can see down below


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/1bbda616c3062600366f783fe7b4b036e2823a19.png

Clicking on that button will open the tournament screen.
Here you can see all the future tournaments, when they will start and how many players are already signed up.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/271c652af1ffec0cf79234d71b0b60e583327353.png

Once you choose a tournament you can press the open button, in this screen, you can have info about the amount of the participation fee and the prize pool.
Last but not least you can sign up for the tourney!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/fc256bcad19467e108b51182277b99e954c5f58d.png

After the beginning of the tournament, you have 15 minutes to play your first games. 
After that time you're out.

We would love to hear your thoughts and your suggestions on future tournaments formats! 
Join us on discord :)

That's all!
Now you are ready to join a tourney and prove your self in the arenas!

notes.title: PLAY AGAINST YOUR FRIENDS! - New Update
notes.notes:
Hey Sumotoris!
We have a big announcement for you!

From the beginning of the Early Access here on Steam, you all asked for the same, very important feature.
We have listened to you!
Our dev team has worked like crazy in the past few months to bring this update to you and finally today we are proud to announce that YOU CAN NOW INVITE YOUR FRIENDS and play against them in Circle of Sumo: Online Rumble!

How does it work?
Well, we redesigned the game's menu a bit.
You will now see your party at the bottom of the screen. 
If you click on the friends list button or on the boxes with the plus symbol, you can invite your friends for parties up to 4 players.

https://media.giphy.com/media/RiWmEvssyX9nbuAc7Y/giphy.gif

At any time you can click on the play button and choose a sumo wrestler and an arena!

https://media.giphy.com/media/Y1vEzVSPbf97r74OwH/giphy.gif

Once all this is done, you can choose between game modes. If you are in a party, you can only go for the free-for-all mode. When all the players have selected both sumotori and arena, they are flagged as ready and the party leader can start the matchmaking!
Don't worry if your party is not made up of 4 players, the game will match you with random players from the internet. No random players from the internet? The game will start with just your friends!

https://media.giphy.com/media/QaHOuY6kSqnAnSgvlA/giphy.gif

That's all for the first sumo-tutorial, now you are ready to challenge your friends in Circle of Sumo: Online Rumble!

[previewyoutube=FhsAfE6vq1o;full][/previewyoutube]

Oh, one last thing!
We made another important change, and it's about the defeat condition.
Many of you noticed that sometimes, even if an opponent was thrown out of the arena before you, you could lose the round. That was because maybe the other player was still "flying" across the map and, until the animation kicked in, they were still considered in play. 
Well, we fixed that! Now the player will be considered defeated as soon they are outside of the ring.


Here we go with the full CHANGELOG:
1.3.7

Added Play With Friends and party management functionalities.
Added Unranked FFA game mode with Play With Friends and variable player count support.
Removed Ranked FFA.
Moved the selection of the game mode after the selection of the sumotori and the arena to better support Play With Friends.
Changed defeat condition: a player is considered defeated as soon as they are outside of the ring instead of waiting for them to slow down and perform the defeat animation.
Decreased charge times for all the sumotoris.
Added buttons to the Banzuke to jump to the first positions and to the player’s position.
Saved emotes key-mappings on the servers. They won’t be lost anymore when using a different device to play the game.
Fixed video options showing only a couple of incorrect resolutions.
Fixed player names with curly braces causing exceptions to be thrown.
Disabled multiple cursors support as it was no longer necessary.
Updated Rewired to solve a bug related to Steam and focus changing.
Fixed the charge bar not emptying when a player cancels their charge.

notes.title: CHANGELOG #4 - 1.2.1
notes.notes:
A new Sumo-Update is now online!

Let's start from the Takarabakos (The boxes), we added a new one!
You can now find Champions and Arenas when you open this new Takarabako.
Yes, even if you don't have the DLC!
The DLC is still the fastest way to have all the players and the arenas selectable.

We have another interesting change, we redesigned the Tower level!
As you know a lot of players like to camp on the tower merlons, but thanks to your feedback
we decided to say no to camping-sumo and now you can't just stand near a merlon. 

Why? 
Because...you know, you are a bit out of shape, and now the merlons are round, the result will be just you sliding and sweating on the brand new convex merlon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/59ecb7b509d819c37d784099d47ec3b241411e18.png


Gamepad-friendly

A lot of players told us that Mouse is a better way to play Circle of Sumo thanks to the aiming system.
Well, we added a cursor showing the direction the player is charging also if you are playing with a gamepad.
We are for equal rights for keyboard-mouse and gamepad users <3

We decided to implement the rankings into the matchmaking system. You will now be able to match players with abilities similar to yours. 
No one is at your level? 
No worries, if no matches are found in a reasonably short amount of time, the system will ignore the skill constraints.

Want to know another thing you can do faster? Counter-move!
We reduced the preparation time of the counter-move to make it fast as the dodge.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36101366/f21de83b1aae96cfd962f3cb657807583ce1d7b7.jpg

Floating names on the Sumotoris head
At the beginning of every match, you will see your name and respective of the other sumotoris.
Now you can rapidly find out who is your worst enemies, or your friend...who knows?

Fixes and changes, the full list of what's new in this update ( You should not read this)


 Added a new Takarabako containing players and arenas.
 Changed the map ‘Tower’ to have convex crenellations that should prevent excessively defensive strategies.
 Modified the skill calculation algorithm to be fairer and more consistent.
 Modified the skill ranges of the ranks to better reflect the ability level of the players.
 Added numbers to the skill ranks’ names to make their order clearer.
 Added skill-based matchmaking. If no matches are found in a reasonably short amount of time, the system will ignore the skill constraints.
 Added players’ names on top of each character at the beginning of each round.
 Added a cursor showing the direction the player is charging towards when a gamepad is used.
 Reduced the preparation time of the counter-move to make it as fast as the dodge.
 Changed ‘cancel’ into ‘ok’ in the message signalling that the player does not have enough money to purchase a Takarabako.
 Added buttons to access the store/items collection from every screen and fixed its transition animation.
 Added coins panel to every screen.
 Added message to indicate that the game does not support versions of Windows below Windows 10.
 Fixed video options panel not showing some resolutions when using them.
 Fixed the button to open a Takarabako remaining active when the player doesn’t have enough money and a message is shown.
 Fixed NullReferenceException in Quantum.Entity.GetTransform2D (Quantum.ShockwaveSystem.ProcessShockwaves).
 Fixed NullReferenceException in UIPopup.Show.
 Fixed UIScoreboard.TryFetchingAgain not working when fetching the backend data fails.
 Fixed the emote binding screen not always processing clicks.
 Fixed NullReferenceException in LocalInput.Update when quitting a match.
 Fixed the bug reported not always working during matches.
 Mitigated connection drops during matches with high latency.



And thaaaaat's all for now!
Enjoy the update, see you in the Arenas!

notes.title: It's not an update, it's a counter update!

1.1.12

 Fixed leaderboard jumping back to the player position after scrolling a few pages

 Fixed leaderboard buttons being interactive before the login was completed. If the user managed to click on them, the game showed some errors

notes.title: A fresh new update!
notes.notes:
Hello you beautiful sumotori!

It's the nerdy code guys here. No marketing supervision at all. Yay!

Well, we just wanted to let you know that we worked hard to deliver you a fresh update just in time for this weekend. We think you'll like it. Less bugs is more fun! 

Changelog
1.1.11


Fixed the matches starting with the wrong number of players (FFA in 3 people or 1v1 in 1 person).
Fixed players sometimes spectating matches instead of playing.
Fixed: if all the alive players in a match got disconnected, the match never ended.
Fixed IndexOutOfRangeException sometimes happening when plugging in a new controller.
Managing all the cases where Photon could get disconnected with a popup and returning to the main menu. This should reduce the time the game appears frozen in the loading screens.
Fixed a rare issue with animations being played in slo-mo when the player got disconnected when performing a belly-bounce.
Fixed NullReferenceExcetion OnLeaderboardLoaded when opening the leaderboard and then quickly pressing retry in the scoreboard screen.
Implemented Steam username change detection to automatically reflect the changes in-game.
Updated the PlayFab SDK used to connect to our backend to the latest version.
Added a “Back soon” badge on the disabled game modes to better indicate that we temporarily disabled them and we will be re-enable them soon.
Fixed the Banzuke being deactivated when the relative game mode was disabled.
